Definition: from G303 (in the sense of reversal) and G4428; to unroll (a scroll or volume):--open.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once: in the synagogue at Nazareth, there was delivered unto Jesus the book of the prophet Isaiah, and when He had opened the book, He found the place where it was written, 'The Spirit of the Lord is upon me.' It is the unrolling of a scroll — the book opened to the exact place, and the reading that followed.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for unrolling carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the opening — the scroll unrolled to Isaiah, and Jesus finding the place where it was written.
